# New: Import a release's own files, such as its cue sheet and rip log

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on [`fix/extras-link-track-files`](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/fix/extras-link-track-files) and merges after it.

With Import Extra Files on, Lidarr imports only extra files named after a track, such as `01 - Song.lrc` beside `01 - Song.flac`. A release's own files, such as `Album.cue` or the rip log, never match a track's name, so they stay in the download folder.

- Once an album's tracks are imported, every file in their download folders that has a wanted extension and that no audio file's name starts goes into the folder the album's tracks share (their deepest common folder), under its own name and byte for byte. Every audio file in those folders counts, so the lyrics of a track that didn't import aren't taken for the release's. A folder gives release files only when each audio file in it came from this album's decisions, imported or not: a folder holding another album's tracks gives none, and neither does a single-file download, which sits in the client's shared folder.
- An audio file with a cue sheet of the same name beside it is an image, not a track, so its `.cue` and `.log` are the release's. After Unpackerr's `split_flac` splits an image, Lidarr matches the image to no track and leaves it in the download, and imports the split tracks, the cue sheet and the rip log. The row has the album and no track file: migration 915 lets `ExtraFiles.TrackFileId` be null, as `MetadataFiles` already allows.
- A release file is never written over an existing file: one an import that doesn't replace kept, one nothing recorded, or a second download folder's file of the same name. It is skipped with a warning. One whose row can't be saved is taken back out of the library (deleted if copied, moved back if moved), so it can't stand in the way of a later import.
- An import that replaces the album's files (every download import does; a manual import when asked to) first sends the previous release's files to the recycle bin, whatever the Import Extra Files setting, as the replaced tracks' own extras go whatever it says. One that doesn't replace keeps them.
- Renaming moves a release file to the folder the album's tracks now share, keeping its name.
- Deleting the album with its files recycles its release files, with its other extras (from `fix/extras-link-track-files`). Removing its track files one at a time, a disk scan finding them gone, or removing the root folder leaves them on disk, until a replacing import or the album's deletion; housekeeping drops their rows once the album is gone.
- Wanted extensions match regardless of case and only after a dot: `log` matches `Album.LOG` but not `Album.backlog`. Before, `log` missed `.LOG` and matched `backlog`, for track-named files too.
- The Import Extra Files help text says so. The extension examples keep develop's text: another image branch adds a key on the next line, and the image's union merge of `en.json` would keep both versions of the line.

Tests, over the real services and test database: release files imported once into the album folder under their names (a UTF-16 cue sheet byte for byte, `.LOG` for `log`), with the track's lyrics still linked to the track; a track that didn't import keeps its lyrics out; a split image's cue sheet and rip log imported; no release files from a folder holding another album's audio or beside a single-file download; a replacing import recycles the previous release's files, also with Import Extra Files off, and one that doesn't replace keeps them; nothing written over an existing file; a file whose row can't be saved taken back out; extension matching by case and after a dot; the migration keeping rows and storing one without a track file; a release file moved with its album's tracks across disc folders, another album's left alone; only the album's own release files recycled, kept when the album's last track file is removed, and recycled when the album is deleted with its files but not without; housekeeping keeping an album's release file and dropping one whose album is gone. Each was broken on purpose and caught by a test.
